items.response:
Glad you landed safely. I don't have the numbers from the pre-booking flight search or the Lafourcade song thing in front of me, so I'll look both up instead of guessing. The flight search would be from when you first asked about Vancouver flights for the August long weekend.
Action: Find the earlier flight search and what it priced, plus the Lafourcade song thing from our earlier chat, and send both so you can show Kabir and Mei.

Happy to. Which place do you want to order from, and what do you want? I don't have a usual order on file here.
Action: Wait for the shop and your order, then place the pickup order for 15 minutes from now and confirm the total with you.

Saved in a private health note: penicillin allergy (hives), and seasonal allergies in May managed with Reactine. I'll surface the allergy if a prescription or appointment comes up.
Action: Save both to a private health note and keep them out of shared notes.

Added Grace's birthday on Thu 19 Nov (her 68th) to the calendar as a yearly event, with a reminder on Thu 5 Nov, two weeks ahead, to sort her gift. Since you're driving up to Ottawa on Fri 13 Nov, that leaves about a week to get it bought and packed.
Action: Create the yearly 19 Nov event for Grace and the 5 Nov gift reminder.

I'll set up in-store pickup at Queen & Logan for Biscuit's food with Sam as the pickup name, after confirming the usual 13.6 kg bag is in stock there today. Slack draft for the payouts team: 'Quick reminder: release freeze runs Thu 12:00 to Mon 09:00 for the bank-partner cutover. Please get anything you need merged before Thursday noon, and reach out if something urgent comes up. Thanks all.' Aisha already has a similar message scheduled for Thu 07:00, so this one is an early heads-up.
Action: Confirm stock and place the pickup order, and save the Slack draft in #payouts-launch without posting it.

Texting Hannah a yes from you: Leo goes to the Chos tonight, she picks up both boys at 3:30 for pizza and a movie, and brings Leo back tomorrow morning in time to walk in with Jun. I'll check tonight's calendar for conflicts first, then put it on the family calendar.
Action: Text Hannah a yes with thanks and add the sleepover to the family calendar (3:30 pickup today, back tomorrow morning for the school walk).

Good tour questions: how many children per teacher in the infant or toddler room, and how long the staff have been there, since turnover says a lot. What a typical day looks like, including naps and outdoor time, and how they help a baby who is still settling in. How they handle illness, allergies and feeding, and what the fees are, including whether they're in the $10-a-day program. Also how long the waitlist is and when a spot could actually start.
Action: Turn these into a short checklist you can text to Marcus to pass on to his sister.

I'll look up rough Air Canada round-trip fares to Vancouver for the August long weekend, no basic economy, aisle seat, with prices in CAD. I'll price it for just you and for you plus Leo, and from Toronto unless you tell me otherwise.
Action: Search Air Canada fares for the long weekend, show the rough cost for one adult and for an adult plus a child in CAD, and note anything that looks better with Aeroplan points.

This morning: the dog walker Felipe (Paws on Pape) is in the pet budget, which puts monthly pet spend at about $729 against a $350 budget. I pulled the six open payouts launch risks into the Notion doc 'Payouts v2 launch risks (2025-11-12)' for tomorrow's standup, with PAY-360 and PAY-366 marked as needing an estimate by 2025-11-14. The October grocery total with the August and September comparison is still running.
Action: Send you the grocery comparison as soon as it's back.

I can work that out, but I don't have the school pickup time or Sam's parents' address here, so I won't guess an arrival time. Friday traffic will matter too.
Action: Check your calendar for next Friday and your notes for the school dismissal time and Sam's parents' address, then send you an estimated arrival time based on a Friday drive.

Use =COUNTIF(D:D,">10000"), which counts every payout over $10,000 in column D, so no need for anything fancier. If you want exactly $10,000 included, use ">=10000", and header text is ignored automatically.
Action: None needed, and your library holds at Pape/Danforth are still waiting until Saturday.

You're right, it used to be January: every Super Bowl through the 2001 season was played in January. It slipped into February after the 2001 season (that year's game was delayed after 9/11) and stayed there as the NFL schedule grew, with the move to 17 games in 2021 pushing it later still. It's on a Sunday because that's the NFL's main game day and the biggest TV audience.
Action: None needed.

Ugh, a packed 504 with a backpack in your face is a rough start to an office day. Whenever you're ready, say the word if you want me to grab the 10:30 Sat 23 May tune-up for Leo's bike at Gears on Gerrard.
Action: Wait for your go on the Gears slot, and for where the team wants the beta feedback log to live.

A chipped front tooth is worth getting seen quickly, so I'll ask for the earliest after-school slot this week and mention it's a chip. If you find the broken piece, bring it with you. I don't have Dr. Lin's address here, so I'll get the travel time from home once I have it.
Action: Look up Dr. Lin's office and contact details, check openings after school this week, and send you the options plus the travel time from home.

I'll line up Nate's revised quote against your numbers after your review. I'm reading the budget as $48,000 total with the 10% contingency inside it, so about $43,636 base and roughly $4,364 of contingency, and I'll show how much of that contingency the revised quote uses. I haven't seen the revised quote yet, so I can't say yet whether he's eating into it.
Action: Find Nate's revised quote in your texts and email, compare it with the reno sheet, and send you a side-by-side with the contingency used; I'll message Nate by text only if I need anything from him.

Welcome back, and glad the drive was fine. Tuesday feeling like a week already is a mood, so go easy on yourself.
Action: Nothing needed; say the word if you want me to pull together what's waiting on you today.

Reminder added for 17:15 to pick up your Shoppers prescription at Queen & Carlaw. Since Tom owns the recurring 1:1, I can't move his series myself, and declining the Thursday ones would send him a decline, so I'd rather not do that. I'll check whether his invite has already updated, and if not, add my own Wednesday 11:30 hold from January 2026 and draft a note asking him to move the series.
Action: Set the 17:15 reminder, check the 1:1 series, add the Wednesday 11:30 hold if needed, and show you the note to Tom before sending.

I'll check Saturday's calendar for conflicts and then text Hannah a yes for 1 to 4. For a rainy afternoon: a build challenge with Lego or cardboard, an obstacle course with couch cushions and a timer, a scavenger hunt around the house, and a movie to wind down before pickup.
Action: Check Saturday afternoon, text Hannah (a text, since she's on shift) that Jun is welcome from 1 to 4, and send you the indoor plan to print or tweak.

What I have is the zellige tile backsplash photos you asked for on Jan 17, when you didn't pick one, and the follow-up request for a few more in white or sage green. Nate needs the decision by Monday, and he prefers texts, so no calls.
Action: Gather both rounds of zellige photos into one board, check your notes for any other inspiration, and once you pick, draft a text to Nate for you to approve.

Try one of these: 'I told my team the budget was balanced, and technically it is, if you round everything to the nearest million.' Or: 'Accountants never get lost, they just follow the paper trail.' Both are clean and crypto-free.
Action: Pick the one you like and I'll tighten it for Friday's standup, or send you a couple more.

I'll build the PC Express cart for Saturday morning pickup, 9:00-10:00 at Loblaws Lakeshore, using no-name brands for the staples: milk, eggs, bread, rice, pasta, bananas, apples, yogurt tubes, cheddar, dish soap, paper towels and the frozen veggie dumplings for Sam. If the PEC trip is a yes tonight, tell me and I'll move the slot.
Action: Build the cart and send it for your review before checkout.

Easy, and a late mug is still on tradition. I'll search for the most ridiculous novelty mugs, ranked by ridiculousness and reviews, and filter to ones that can reach Kabir in Vancouver within a few days.
Action: Search for the options, show you the top picks with price and delivery time, and not order anything until you choose; I'll confirm Kabir's delivery address first.

Nut-free lunch ideas: ham or turkey and cheese pinwheels, pasta salad with cucumber and cheese cubes, mini bagel pizzas, a build-your-own lunch box with crackers, cheese and fruit, and plain or chicken quesadillas cut in triangles. I'd check every label, since 'nut-aware' isn't nut-free. I don't have what you asked about Biscuit and the ambulance, so I'll look it up in our earlier chats.
Action: Look up what you asked about Biscuit and the ambulance and send it, plus a printable version of the five lunches.

I don't see a confirmation in front of me for your or Leo's November appointments, so I'll check rather than assume.
Action: Search your email and texts for the dentist's confirmations for your and Leo's November appointments, and if there's none, draft a message asking the office to confirm.

That is a very committed snore. At least Diego knows the sound of a dog hard at work.
Action: None needed.

Here's a draft: 'Hi Hannah, thank you so much for the shortbread! Leo ate four, so I think it was a hit. That was so kind of you.'
Action: Show you this draft and send it to Hannah once you say go, or tweak it first.

I'll search for 3-night hotel options in Drumheller for march break, with prices in CAD, and check the Royal Tyrrell Museum's admission for a child Leo's age. I need your check-in day within the week of the 16th and Leo's age to get the right ticket category. I won't book anything, since you want to approve any purchase over $100.
Action: Search Drumheller hotels for 3 nights and the Tyrrell child admission price, show you the options in CAD, and ask before booking anything.

That sounds like a perfect porch moment, enjoy the coffee. I'll leave the career day talk for later; it's on Tue 31 Mar at 9:15, so there's time.
Action: Check back with you later today about the career day talk.

On it. I'll build a focus playlist of Khruangbin and A. R. Rahman instrumentals for tomorrow, and swap spin for strength training at the Leslieville YMCA on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 6:15 am with a 'home by 7:15' end so Sam can leave for school. That makes tomorrow, Tue 13 Jan, your first session, and it's an office day, so you'll want an early start.
Action: End the spin series, add the Tuesday and Thursday strength series starting tomorrow with the 7:15 home-by constraint, and send you the playlist.

I'll find the Purina Pro Plan Sensitive Skin & Stomach salmon formula and check the listing's flavour and ingredients before ordering, so no chicken-based variant slips in. I'll match the bag size to your last order.
Action: Check your last order for the size, verify the listing says salmon and isn't chicken-based, then place the reorder if it matches exactly, otherwise show you the options first.

I'd need to see how much you actually spend there before answering, and I don't have those numbers in front of me. A membership usually pays off when your yearly savings and any rebate beat the annual fee.
Action: Pull your Costco purchases from the last 12 months and the membership fee, compare them, and tell you whether renewing makes sense.

I don't have the rink conditions or Saturday's forecast in front of me, so I'll check before you promise Leo. Natural ice depends on the temperature, so it's worth a look closer to the day.
Action: Check the City's rink status for Withrow and Saturday afternoon's forecast, tell you if it looks okay, and suggest a backup rink if it doesn't; also remind you tomorrow to snap a photo of the insurance letter.

Added to your running stats: Toronto Waterfront Half Marathon, October 19, 2025, finish time 2:04:37. I'll set a reminder in early December to put together your yearly recap.
Action: Add the race to your running stats and schedule the December recap reminder; send you what the recap will cover once I see the rest of your logged runs.

Pulling those now, titles and status only.
Action: Query Linear for your open tickets tagged payouts-ga and send back just the title and status for each.
